title: while/repeat hitting max_iterations reports success — runaway loops truncate work silently
existing_state: Both loop commands hardcode DefaultMaxIterations = 10000 (Services/Scripting/Commands/WhileCommand.cs:14, RepeatCommand.cs:15). When the cap is reached they emit a single Warning-type output line and return Success (WhileCommand.cs:105-110 returns {Success = true}; RepeatCommand.cs:85-90 likewise). A while whose condition never flips — e.g. polling a device that never comes back, or a typo'd variable that makes the condition perpetually true — therefore stops mid-work and the run, job history, and any notify-on-failure logic all see a green result. The per-step max_iterations override exists (WhileCommand.cs:30-32, RepeatCommand.cs:31-33) but there is no way to make cap-exhaustion fail the step.
recommendation: Add an on_max_iterations: fail | warn option on while/repeat (and foreach if it shares the pattern). Defaulting to fail is the honest behavior; if back-compat matters, keep warn as default but emit it as Error-type output and set a _loop_truncated context variable plus a flag on CommandResult so the Flow Canvas run summary and job history can show 'loop hit cap' instead of a clean pass. The change is localized to the two cap checks.
user_benefit: A stuck polling loop in an overnight scheduled job becomes a red failed run with a clear reason, instead of a green run that quietly did 10,000 useless iterations and skipped everything after the real work was supposed to happen.

evidence.note: hardcoded 10000 default; cap reached = Warning + Success=true
same pattern in the do-while variant
